T-001.Title: Catalog completeness: review/gate namespaces and makeFinding visibility (F10)

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Red-first: append or inject a production emission of review.attempt-pair-unsubstantiated (object form or makeFinding) without a src/lint/catalog.ts entry; bun test src/lint/catalog.test.ts must fail today (F10 probe). After the fix the same emission stays green without any lint-catalog entry. Assert through the catalog.test surface, not a private helper return value.

Completeness routes review.* codes to REVIEW_CATALOG and gate.* codes to the gate catalog — never getExactLintIssueGuide. Discriminating negative: a new review.* code must not be reported as a lint-catalog orphan; a new unguided lint.* code must still fail completeness (lint path unchanged).

Scanner recognizes makeFinding(code, file, message, …) positional form so the thirteen existing review codes become visible. Both namespace routing and makeFinding visibility are required; either alone fails this criterion. Expect a backlog of pre-existing review codes without exact REVIEW_CATALOG guides: place them on a frozen, commented allowlist in catalog.test.ts, report the list to the authority, and do not mass-author guides in this task. Newly introduced codes from later tasks in this bundle must not sit on that allowlist (T-005 precedent: new codes get exact guides).

Red-first: CLI cursor advance --open-epoch --from T-001 --to T-001 (and library advanceCursor with from/to NaN, 0, -1, 1.5, and from>to) exits 0 and writes corrupt run/* today — capture that failure mode in a regression that fails on pre-fix code. After fix: each invalid case exits non-zero, writes no run/* file, and the error message names positive integer event ids and states that task ids are not event ids. Valid --from 1 --to 10 still opens. Assert via CLI/library exit behaviour and absence of written files, not only an internal validator return.

T-003.Title: Orphan inventory for both silent-skip classes (D8.7 / F8.2)

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Red-first: a temp run/ containing NaN-T-001-opened.xml (EVENT_FILENAME :459 miss) and a well-named file whose XML id is non-integer or non-positive (:470 class) yields empty or incomplete visibility through listLooseEvents alone; the new parallel orphan inventory must report both classes. listLooseEvents remains the ordered positive-integer reader (D8.7) — do not widen it to return orphans in its primary list. Discriminating negatives: :470-only fix leaves NaN-* unreported; :459-only fix leaves non-integer-id well-named files unreported. Assert through the exported orphan inventory API (or recover diagnose once T-004 exists, but this task's unit surface must name both classes before recover lands).

Red-first: ngrace cursor recover --change C-ID is absent or non-functional today — regression fails until the subcommand exists. On a *copy* of the F8.1 shape (NaN-* opened with Allocation from="NaN" to="NaN", plus valid loose integer events, no valid allocation — never the live C-TOKEN-INTEGRITY ledger), recover without --fix reports: unrecoverable orphan (no recoverable event id), missing valid covering allocation, the integer loose-event range, and that fold is blocked. Assert via CLI text/exit (or stable JSON fields), consuming the orphan inventory from T-003. Do not mutate C-TOKEN-INTEGRITY/run/.

T-005.Title: recover --fix covering allocation and single-controller auto-open (P0.6)

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Red-first: on a *copy* of the F8.1 shape, fold fails with no Allocation found before --fix. After recover --fix extend-allocation (or create-covering under the same flag): a recorded ledger-visible opened/Allocation spans the valid integer loose ids and fold succeeds for that stream. After --fix the NaN-* orphan file still exists on disk and recover still reports it as an unrecoverable orphan — a test that only asserts "fold succeeds" without the orphan's continued presence and continued diagnosis fails this criterion (deletion would pass that weaker bar; D8.3 / F8.1). Tests never call --fix on the live C-TOKEN-INTEGRITY ledger; that remains a separate authorized act by the authority.

Red-first: loose integer events, no valid open allocation, at most one distinct worker value → fold (or the designated auto-open surface) fails or dead-ends today; after fix it synthesizes a retroactive covering opened (A29.2/F1: bounds derived from inventory; explicit command is the apply). When more than one distinct worker value appears, auto-open refuses and demands explicit epoch open (D8.2). Multi-worker ranges are never silently fabricated. Assert via CLI/library behaviour and resulting Allocation children.

Red-first: ngrace review --change C-ID (or runReview with attempt fixtures) on a fail→pass pair whose non-test ObservedWriteScope digests are identical emits no attempt-pair finding today — write that failing regression first. After fix: warning-severity ReviewFinding review.attempt-pair-unsubstantiated (or the agreed code) registered in REVIEW_CATALOG with an exact guide (not on the F10 backlog allowlist). Non-test = paths not ending in .test.ts/.test.js, intersected with plan ObservedWriteScope. Corpus shapes from C-TOKEN event digests (read-only fixtures or copies): T-001 2→3 and T-002 6→7 raise; T-005 16→17 (test-only) also raises (F9.3). cursor attempt stays quiet at write time. Assert through review finding codes/severity, not internal digest helpers alone.

Clearing requires a recorded free-text reason, not a boolean flag (D8.6). REVIEW_CATALOG guide instructs the reviewer to record the reason on ngrace gate verdict --note keyed by the finding's stable findingId. Finding emission includes a stable findingId suitable for that note. A path that only marks "reviewed" without reason text fails this criterion. Do not invent a new finding-clearance ledger schema in this task; stop and report if gate verdict notes cannot carry the reason (D8.6).

T-007.Title: status distinguishes open vs folded epochs (D8.8)

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Red-first: on a temp project with a healthy open epoch (from=1 to=N, progress recorded, no folded Epoch-N), ngrace status presents bare epochs=0 or omits open activity while cursor show reports Epoch ≥ 1 — capture that misreport in a failing regression. After fix: status distinguishes folded epoch count from open (unfolded) epochs so an in-progress run is not indistinguishable from a change with no cursor activity. After fold, folded count reflects Epoch-N wrappers. Assert via formatStatusText / collectProjectStatus fields a reviewer can print, not only an internal counter rename.

Full suite green: F8 NaN open+work+fold on a temp copy, bounds matrix, both orphan classes, recover diagnose and preserve-orphan --fix, auto-open single- vs multi-worker, attempt-pair T-001/T-002/T-005 shapes, F10 probe, status open-vs-folded.
